reasons: Internal control and audit (3 of 4): three of material weakness, adverse ICFR opinion, auditor change and disagreement are present. That almost certainly means a material weakness with an adverse ICFR opinion, plus either an auditor change or a disagreement. This is the strongest single indicator of misstatement risk on the card.

Numeric warning signals (2 of 4 computable): two quantitative screens (Beneish M, Dechow F, accruals > 3% of assets, OCF < 0.8x net income) are triggered. This points to earnings quality problems or accrual-driven earnings, which matches the control weaknesses.
Financial pressure (2 of 4): two pressure indicators (going concern, covenant problem, revenue/EPS-linked incentive pay, capital raise) give both motive and incentive to manage results.
Management turnover (1 of 2): a CEO/CFO change or an interim CFO, together with weak controls, raises the risk of a breakdown in the financial reporting process.

Transaction complexity (4 of 8): half of the complexity flags are present (e.g. over-time revenue, contract assets, related parties, acquisition, inventory write-down, customer concentration). This gives many judgement areas where misstatement can happen.

Mitigating: Prior-period corrections (0 of 3) and Investigations and litigation (0 of 3) are clean. No restatement, SEC inquiry or class action has surfaced yet, which keeps the score below the highest range. Note: the card gives only area-level counts, not individual F/R items, so the reasons cite areas.
